## ADR-0001: Store the failed-attempt count and lock time in the Auth Database
status: Accepted
date: 2026-09-15
elements: [authService, authDb]

Context:
The account must lock after 5 failed logins in a row (BR-001) and unlock after
15 minutes. The Auth Service runs on several servers, so a count kept in one
server's memory would be wrong.

Decision:
The Auth Service stores failed_attempts and locked_until on the account row in
the Auth Database. Each failed login adds 1 to failed_attempts. On the 5th, it
sets locked_until = now + 15 minutes. A successful login sets failed_attempts
to 0 (BR-002).

Consequences:
- The count is correct no matter which server handles the login.
- Tests can set up a locked account by writing these two fields through a
  test fixture, instead of waiting 15 minutes.


## ADR-0002: The lock is enforced by the Auth Service, not by the Login UI
status: Accepted
date: 2026-09-20
elements: [authService, loginUI]

Context:
A lock that only the browser enforces can be bypassed by calling the API directly.

Decision:
The Auth Service decides whether an account is locked. When it is, POST /auth/login
returns 423 Locked with the message "Your account is locked. Try again in 15 minutes."
The Login UI only displays the message it receives.

Consequences:
- The lock rules are tested at API level; the UI tests only check the message is shown.
- Changing the message text needs a change to the Auth Service, not the UI.
